entries.prose: Level 3 of the faith ladder: the ordained priest or priestess who keeps a hof's rites.

entries.description: The high priest who consecrates a hof and performs the great blót at a season's turning, in the seven faiths of the Ten that keep it.
entries.note: _hof-_ "the temple building" + the kept _godi_ / _gydja_ — keeper of a named hof; both forms stand in the name because the standing is one
entries.prose: Level 4 of the faith ladder: consecrates a hof and performs the great blót at a season's turning.

entries.description: The sovereign standing of the Jarldom of Stormveld, held by a jarl elected from among his peers.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, built on the kept word _jarl_: Stormveld seats no king, so its sovereign standing is a jarl raised above jarls rather than a crown
entries.prose: The sovereign standing of the Jarldom of Stormveld, held by a jarl elected from among his peers rather than by a royal clan's acclamation.

entries.description: Full clan membership, holding odal land and a voice at the ting, in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld.
entries.note: _bóndi_ — a kept word of the tongue for the odal-holding freeman; level 3, where the ting enfranchises the commons, and the word stands rather than drifting
entries.prose: Level 3 of the civic ladder, the full clan member: holds his own odal land by inheritance, bears arms, and speaks at the ting in a ruling that binds the jarl over him.

entries.description: The nobility, holding a province of the king and commanding its hersvaldar, in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld.
entries.note: _jarl_ — a kept word of the tongue, named among the setting's own; level 6, the nobility holding a province of the king
entries.prose: Level 6 of the civic ladder: holds a province by the king's grant, commands its hersvaldar, and answers to the king for its peace — a grant the crown can move, unlike a bóndi's odal land.

entries.description: The sovereign, chosen from the royal clans and acclaimed at the ting, in the five kingdoms.
entries.note: the standing is written in the reader's tongue, as the Lawspeaker and the Queen are; the Nordmal _konungr_ stands behind the shortcode, and the faith ladder's own Konungr is retired, so the word is left to the polity alone
entries.prose: Level 7 of the civic ladder: chosen from the royal clans and acclaimed at the ting, holding the realm on the assembly's continuing consent, which can refuse to hand his arm-ring back.

entries.description: Outlawed at the ting and set beyond the law's protection, in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld.
entries.note: _níding_ — the north's own word for a man set outside the law, named in the tongue's kept words; the ladder's level 0, cast out, and the word stands rather than drifting
entries.prose: Level 0 of the Nordmal civic ladder in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld: outlawed at the ting, killing him draws no penalty, and a hall that shelters him answers for it.

entries.description: Owned outright, owing labor rather than rent and holding no voice at the ting, in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld.
entries.note: _thrall_ — a kept word of the tongue, the man owned outright; level 1, the lowest standing the law still describes, and unfreedom is a rank because the law treats him apart
entries.prose: Level 1 of the civic ladder: owned rather than born free, owing labour itself rather than rent, barred from arms and unheard at the ting.

entries.description: A common warrior of a Compact-signed company, testified by his captain, in Málalidabandalag.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the standing is the oath a captain testifies to, so the name says sworn and says of what
entries.prose: Level 1 of Málalidabandalag: a common warrior of a Compact-signed company, testified by his captain.

entries.description: Expelled from the Compact by Council vote, the bronze thumb-ring surrendered, in Málalidabandalag.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the Compact states the condition as the discharge and the surrender of the bronze thumb-ring
entries.prose: Level 0 of Málalidabandalag: expelled from the Compact by Council vote, the bronze thumb-ring surrendered.

entries.description: Swears the Compact before the Council of the Hall and wears the bandalagshringr, in Málalidabandalag.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: signing the Compact before the Council is the act that confers the standing, and the bandalagshringr is its mark
entries.prose: Level 3 of Málalidabandalag: swears the Compact before the Council of the Hall and wears the bandalagshringr.

entries.description: The full member of the Order of the Giant's Children, admitted by a rite of ordeal and theological examination.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, from Thursbörn's own theology: the full member is born of the founding wound, admitted by ordeal and examination
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Order of the Giant's Children: the full member, admitted by a rite of ordeal and theological examination.

entries.description: The working warden of the Order of the Green Wardens, holding a station or riding circuit relief.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, from the order's own name: Grönverdir's working member is a sworn guardian
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Order of the Green Wardens: the working warden, holding a station or riding circuit relief.

entries.description: The full member of the Order of the Storm-Speakers, acting on the order's behalf across the Nordlands.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, from the order's own name: a Storm-Speaker's full member is a sworn speaker
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Order of the Storm-Speakers: acts on the order's behalf across the Nordlands.

entries.description: The warrior-judge of the Order of the Sworn Hand, riding circuit to render and enforce rulings under the white wand.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, from the order's own name: Eidhönd's full member is a sworn hand, and the order's title carries the Nordmal form
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Order of the Sworn Hand: the warrior-judge who rides circuit to render and enforce rulings under the white wand.

entries.description: Convicted of breaking the truth of the recital, the arm-ring broken at the next Skaldating, in the Skalds' Circle.
entries.note: the reader's tongue around the ring the Circle gives: the condition is named by the breaking, which is what the Skaldating does
entries.prose: Level 0 of the Skalds' Circle: convicted of breaking the truth of the recital, the arm-ring broken at the next Skaldating.

entries.description: Acclaimed by his peers when his composed sagas enter the standing repertoire, in the Skalds' Circle.
entries.note: _stórald_ "the great telling" + _-stjóri_ "one who directs a thing" — the master whose composed sagas enter the standing repertoire
entries.prose: Level 4 of the Skalds' Circle: acclaimed by his peers when his composed sagas enter the standing repertoire.

entries.description: Sworn keeper of a hall's record, entitled to food, shelter and safe passage at any hall, in the Skalds' Circle.
entries.note: _skald_ — a kept word of the tongue, named among the setting's own; the sworn keeper of a hall's record
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Skalds' Circle: sworn keeper of a hall's record, entitled to food, shelter and safe passage at any hall.

entries.description: A master's pupil for ten to fifteen years, entitled to present a drápa, in the Skalds' Circle.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the standing is a pupillage of ten to fifteen years, and the Circle names it plainly
entries.prose: Level 1 of the Skalds' Circle: a master's pupil for ten to fifteen years, entitled to present a drápa.

entries.description: One of the six who follow Dágulf Véthar, held by fear of the leader and the absence of better options, in the Blackpine Wolves.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the band has one standing and no word for it, so the name states membership and nothing more
entries.prose: The single standing of the Blackpine Wolves: one of the six who follow Dágulf Véthar, held by fear of the leader and the absence of better options.

entries.description: Taken in war or bought at the river-landings, answering to the mistress of a household about everything, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: the reader's tongue for a Varokhi standing, governed by that language's rule rather than Nordmal's
entries.prose: Level 1 of the Vrystwald Tribes: taken in war or bought at the river-landings, answering to the mistress of a household about everything.

entries.description: Head of a clan or tribe by prowess, wisdom and the warriors' support, and not by descent, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: the reader's tongue for a Varokhi standing: the tribes choose by prowess, wisdom and the warriors' support rather than descent
entries.prose: Level 5 of the Vrystwald Tribes: head of a clan or tribe by prowess, wisdom and the warriors' support, and not by descent.

entries.description: Cast out by their own kin and claimed by none, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: the reader's tongue for a Varokhi standing; Varokhi is its own tongue and Nordmal's rules do not govern its ranks
entries.prose: Level 0 of the Vrystwald Tribes: cast out by their own kin and claimed by none.

entries.description: Of a kindred's blood, entitled to its protection, its feud and its share, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: the reader's tongue for a Varokhi standing: the kindred's blood is what the standing is
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Vrystwald Tribes: of a kindred's blood, entitled to its protection, its feud and its share.

entries.description: Senior of a lineage, whose memory of custom and precedent settles what the young dispute, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: the reader's tongue for a Varokhi standing: seniority in a lineage, not an office
entries.prose: Level 4 of the Vrystwald Tribes: senior of a lineage, whose memory of custom and precedent settles what the young dispute.

entries.description: Free and of no kin, sheltered by a household without being of its blood, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: the reader's tongue for a Varokhi standing: sheltered by a household without being of its blood
entries.prose: Level 2 of the Vrystwald Tribes: free and of no kin, sheltered by a household without being of its blood.

entries.description: One of the company, carrying a charge and a share of the kill, in Wuldjagâr erund Gárskald.
entries.note: the reader's tongue for a Varokhi standing: the company has one word for its members and it is the work they do
entries.prose: Level 3 of Wuldjagâr erund Gárskald: one of the company, carrying a charge and a share of the kill.

entries.description: Recently inducted and still learning the ways, watched for signs of weakness, in Wuldjagâr erund Gárskald.
entries.note: the reader's tongue for a Varokhi standing, governed by that language's rule rather than Nordmal's
entries.prose: Level 1 of Wuldjagâr erund Gárskald: recently inducted and still learning the ways, watched for signs of weakness.

entries.note: eth spelling of the Compact's own name, used throughout the import; the name itself stands and is on the keep-list, so only the spelling moves — the romanisation rule writes a plain d where the import wrote an eth. The note's shortcode and address are unaffected, and both halves state so.

entries.description: Elder-trained fighters of Bjartr's will.
entries.note: the bright blade, from `bjart-` (bright) and `-brandr` (a brand, either a firebrand or a blade). Eldingsekr was built from `elding-` and `-sekr`, neither of which the element lexicon publishes, so the compound rule refused it; the lawful coinage says the same thing from published stock, and the English phrase the faith note glossed it with is kept as the alias: the one body in Bjartr's service built for battle, carrying the elder races' training as a blade of his light.

entries.description: The rare standing between the elder races and mortals.
entries.note: the age's voice, from `aldar-` (an age's) and `-mál` (speech, and the voice a body speaks with). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Bjartr's faith note kept as its alias: the standing speaks between the elder races and mortals, so the name is the voice the elder age speaks with.

entries.description: Healing and counsel in Bjartr's light.
entries.note: the bright hand, from `bjart-` (bright) and `-hönd` (a hand). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Bjartr's faith note kept as its alias: healers and counselors who tend a wound and a troubled dream as one care, so the hand that carries Bjartr's light.

entries.description: Warriors sworn to Eidgar's heaviest oaths.
entries.note: the oath-wards, from `eid-` (an oath sworn at a spear-point) and `-verdir` (wards, keepers). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Eidgar's faith note kept as its alias: warriors under oaths heavier than a soldier's, sworn to the defense of the faith and the hofs where its tings sit.

entries.description: Witnesses and mediators of Eidgar's sworn oaths.
entries.note: the oath-ring, from `eid-` (an oath sworn at a spear-point) and `-ringr` (a ring, and a circle of sworn men). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Eidgar's faith note kept as its alias: priests who witness an oath and keep its memory, a circle of sworn men answering to neither side of a quarrel.

entries.description: Combat and justice at Eidgar's hofs.
entries.note: the law's blade, from `lög-` (the law as it is recited) and `-brandr` (a brand, either a firebrand or a blade). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Eidgar's faith note kept as its alias: priests who hear a dispute at the hof where the ting sits and draw the blade that enforces the ruling.

entries.description: Eidgar's fighting order of honorable combat.
entries.note: the oath-champions, from `eid-` (an oath sworn at a spear-point) and `-káppar` (champions). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Eidgar's faith note kept as its alias: the faith's elite fighting order, the arm a ting's ruling calls on when it needs one.

entries.description: Body and soul tended at Fródvin's infirmaries.
entries.note: the hall's friends, from `hallar-` (a great hall's) and `-vinir` (friends). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Fródvin's faith note kept as its alias: indoor and constant work at the valley infirmaries, the sick tended and the distressed comforted as a household's own would be.

entries.description: Mediation and harmony in Fródvin's name.
entries.note: the peace-bearer, from `fród-` (the peace that wisdom buys) and `-beri` (one who bears a thing). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Fródvin's faith note kept as its alias: mediators who carry Fródvin's peace into a quarrel before it reaches the ting.

entries.description: Herb-lore and healing in Fródvin's service.
entries.note: the green hand, from `grön-` (green, and growing) and `-hönd` (a hand). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Fródvin's faith note kept as its alias: herbalists who keep the sacred groves and the herb-lore Fródvin's healing depends on.

entries.description: Náhild's doctrine spread through fear.
entries.note: the corpse-speakers, from `ná-` (a corpse) and `-maelendir` (ones that speak). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias: they carry Náhild's doctrine beyond her hidden hofs by speaking it where a public blót could never reach.

entries.description: Guardians and inquisitors of Náhild's hidden hofs.
entries.note: the corpse-wards, from `ná-` (a corpse) and `-verdir` (wards, keepers). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias: the cult's own inquisitors, guarding her hidden hofs and the rites kept inside them.

entries.description: Náhild's elite assassins.
entries.note: the night-goers, from `nótt-` (night) and `-gengir` (ones that go). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias: her assassins, whose killings are chosen for the fear they spread as much as for the target.

entries.description: Náhild's hidden cult of the Eye of the Void.
entries.note: the corpse-end, from `ná-` (a corpse) and `-lok` (a close, an end). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias: the hidden cult of the ending, widening the Eye of the Void's reach where no outsider can see the work.

entries.description: The pursuit and keeping of Ódvar's knowledge.
entries.note: the kin of thought, from `hug-` (thought) and `-aett` (a kin reckoned together). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Ódvar's faith note kept as its alias: the most learned of Ódvar's faithful, reckoned together as one body and keeping the libraries at its temples.

entries.description: Rune-lore and divination in Ódvar's service.
entries.note: the raven-rune, from `hrafn-` (a raven) and `-rún` (a rune). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Ódvar's faith note kept as its alias: rune-lore and divination, the staves cast for warbands, jarls and households who need counsel a blót does not supply.

entries.description: Diplomacy and persuasion for Sólrún's faith.
entries.note: the gold-speech, from `gull-` (gold) and `-mál` (speech, and the voice a body speaks with). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Sólrún's faith note kept as its alias: the voice Sólrún's faith speaks with in dealings no blunter envoy could carry.

entries.description: Guardians of Sólrún's sacred wealth.
entries.note: the gold-wards, from `gull-` (gold) and `-verdir` (wards, keepers). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Sólrún's faith note kept as its alias: they hold the gold given away at her rites in trust and answer for every coin that passes a hof's doors.

entries.description: Love and beauty counseled in Sólrún's name.
entries.note: the sun's friends, from `sól-` (the sun) and `-vinir` (friends). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Sólrún's faith note kept as its alias: trained in love and beauty and set at the courts of the powerful, who seek Sólrún's favor through them.

entries.description: A militant order guarding Svartbrandr's forges.
entries.note: the fire-wards, from `eld-` (fire) and `-verdir` (wards, keepers). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Svartbrandr's faith note kept as its alias: they stand watch over a forge-hof through its Fire-Weeks and answer a threat with the same flame the rite uses.

entries.description: Svartbrandr's elite warriors of the forge-hofs.
entries.note: the fire-wolf, from `eld-` (fire) and `-úlfr` (a wolf). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Svartbrandr's faith note kept as its alias: elite warriors known through the forge-hofs for a ferocity the god's own ordeals are built to prove.

entries.description: Fire mastered for Svartbrandr's forges.
entries.note: the smith-fire, from `smid-` (a smith) and `-eldr` (fire). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Svartbrandr's faith note kept as its alias: blacksmiths and forge-masters who tend the bellows keeping a forge-hof's ordeals burning.

entries.description: Thrúnvald's fighting order of hammer-warriors.
entries.note: the hammer-warriors, from `hamar-` (a hammer) and `-drengir` (warriors). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Thrúnvald's faith note kept as its alias: the faith's fighting order, wielding war-hammers in defense of the coastal hofs and the ships blessed from them.

entries.description: Combat and protection at Thrúnvald's coastal hofs.
entries.note: the thunder-shield, from `thrumu-` (thunder) and `-skjöldr` (a shield). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Thrúnvald's faith note kept as its alias: priests trained in combat and protection, standing guard over a coastal hof's stores and its people.

entries.description: Naval combat trained at sea for Thrúnvald.
entries.note: the sea-plate, from `haf-` (the open sea) and `-skel` (a shell, and a plate of iron). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Thrúnvald's faith note kept as its alias: fighters drilled at sea rather than ashore into masters of naval combat and the defense of a ship under way.

entries.description: A militant order guarding Vélgrímr's temples.
entries.note: the troop of guile, from `vél-` (a wile) and `-skari` (a troop). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Vélgrímr's faith note kept as its alias: a militant order guarding his hidden temples by stealth and strategy, since open force would break the secrecy it defends.

entries.description: Illusion and disguise in Vélgrímr's service.
entries.note: the cloud-mask, from `ský-` (cloud) and `-grímr` (a mask). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Vélgrímr's faith note kept as its alias: priests of illusion and disguise, moving through Malagna's ports under a face not their own.

entries.description: Poison-trained fighters of Vélgrímr.
entries.note: the wyrm's point, from `orm-` (a wyrm) and `-geir` (a spear). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Vélgrímr's faith note kept as its alias: they fight by poison as much as by blade, carrying venom prepared at the hidden hofs of Malagna's ports.

entries.description: Sólrún's sworn women, wealth made and given away.
entries.note: the ring-sisters, from `hring-` (a ring given at a hall) and `-systur` (sisters). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Sólrún's faith note kept as its alias: Sólrún's sworn women, making wealth and giving it away, armed at a feast-hall's door and keeping its ledgers alike. The name already stood in the faith's prose and the note carries it unchanged.

entries.description: Put out of a devotional order of the faiths of the Ten, forfeiting its shelter and its purpose alike.
entries.note: the sworn band's outlaw, from `drótt-` (a war-band sworn to one man) and `-vargr` (an outlaw, a wolf in the law's eye). The three standings every one of the twenty-nine shares are built on one element, so the ladder reads as one, as Grönvördr and Eldri Grönvördr do. A closing that names what a member has become is not an office suffix by § _Ranks, offices and orders_, which is why this one is a plain compound where the other two take office suffixes — the same shape Sárborinn carries. The two single-word aliases go: an alias is an English phrase that says what a thing is.

entries.description: The ordinary member of a devotional order of the faiths of the Ten, holding the least standing it confers.
entries.note: a man of the sworn band, from `drótt-` (a war-band sworn to one man) and `-madr` (a man holding a station). The alias is a phrase rather than the bare word, which an alias may not be.

entries.description: The leading standing of a devotional order of the faiths of the Ten, holding its fullest claim on what it confers.
entries.note: the master of the sworn band, from `drótt-` (a war-band sworn to one man) and `-stjóri` (the master of a thing), the office suffix § _Ranks, offices and orders_ gives to the one office of a muster's or a household's master.

entries.description: What Hugaett calls its members, the most learned of Ódvar's faithful and the keepers of its libraries.
entries.note: from `hug-` (thought) and `-fadir` (the father of a hof). A kept word is not an element, so no compound is built from `seidr`, and the half-English form was unbuildable twice over. The gendered pair follows Godi and Gydja, and `-fadir` and `-módir` are the one gendered pair the element tables publish; the order keeps its libraries at its temples, which is the hof the pair answers for.
